title: Utah expands healthcare AI sandbox with August AI, Nolla Health pilots, adds third-party evaluators
source_used: Medical Daily (pool item is Fierce Healthcare, blocked here)
key_facts: Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy posted a list of six outside evaluators: Coalition for Health AI, Stanford's Clinical Excellence Research Center, Clarion AI Partners, mpathic, Vega Health and Glacis Technologies.
The six evaluators signed one-year agreements between August and early October 2026.
The companies being evaluated pay the evaluators directly; the state says it pays nothing for evaluations.
Fees have not been disclosed, and the state has not said which evaluator will review which pilot.
Evaluators must certify independence, report patient safety concerns to the state and allow state audits; a false certification can halt a pilot.
Utah's sandbox was created under a 2024 law, Senate Bill 149 (Artificial Intelligence Policy Act), and lets companies test AI tools under agreements that ease some rules in exchange for monitoring.
Pilots on the state list include Nolla Health (acne), August AI (prescription refills) and Expect Fitness (pelvic floor and postpartum physical therapy).
Results of the pilots have not been published.
